Order 
The appellant, namely, Dharmraj Singh in Cr.A. No.13458/2024 and the appellant - Seeta Devi in CRA No. 11410/2025 have filed these criminal appeals under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by orders dated 05.10.2024 and 19.11.2025 passed in SCATR No.56/2024 by the Special Judge under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Sidhi, MP whereby their regular bail applications have been rejected.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellants that the present appellant - Dharmraj Singh is in custody since 26.06.2024 and the appellant Seeta Devi is in custody since 01.07.2024.
It is further submitted that as per the prosecution case, it is alleged that the prosecutrix was taken away on 28.12.2023 and she was recovered on 03.05.2024 but the FIR was lodged on 31.05.2024.
The delay in lodging the FIR is not explained by the prosecution which is fatal for the prosecution case.

It is contended that during this period of five months, the prosecutrix remained resided with the present appellants but she never opposed and not intimated anyone about the incident nor she complained about the act of the present appellants to anyone.
So far as recovery is concerned, only Rs.2,000/- is recovered from appellant - Seeta Devi whereas the mobile phone which is recovered from the appellant Dharmraj is not related with the present case.

As far as registration of other three criminal cases against Dharmraj and one other case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70247 3 CRA-11410-2025 against the appellant - Seeta Devi is concerned, it is contended that they have been falsely implicated in those cases.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix is a major lady.
The present appellants are in custody for around one a half year.
DNA Test is not conducted while FSL report is negative in respect of the present appellants.
They are ready and willing to abide by all the terms and stringent conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel pray for grant of bail to the appellants.
4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail applications/appeals and prayed for their rejection.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6 . Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is inclined to release the present appellants on bail.

Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, both the appeals are allowed and it is directed that appellants be released on bail upon their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.
8 . Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE ks Seeta Devi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58844489/
